structure: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (2018), one document, grade bands K-2 (e), 3-5 (i), 6-8 (m), 9-12 (h); no grade-specific courses. Front matter (foreword, Section I approach, Section II definitions/structure/strand descriptions) is backup; the At-A-Glance page lists the standard statements of all six strands. Section III is a set of landscape tables, one page per Standard (or per continued learning priorities), by Content Area (Inq inquiry, BH behavioral sciences, Econ, Geog, Hist, PS political science). Code SS.<Area><standard#>.<learning priority letter>.<band or grade suffix>, e.g. SS.Econ1.a.1 (K-2 band, suggested grade 1), SS.Hist1.a.m (middle), .h (high). Each table has a Learning Priority first column (spanning all bands) and four band columns K-2/3-5/6-8/9-12; indicator text is extracted as one unit containing the code plus full sentence, a duplicate code-only cell and then word-wrapped text fragments in the cell column. Column indexes differ per table, so the C index to band map was set per page from header row positions: default pages C1-C2 learning priority, C3-C5 K-2, C6-C8 3-5, C9-C11 6-8, C12-C14 9-12; page 35 (Econ2 cont) C1 LP, C2-C3 K-2, C4-C6 3-5, C7-C9 6-8, C10-C12 9-12; pages 39-41 (Econ4 cont) C1 LP, C2 K-2, C3 3-5, C4 6-8, C5-C6 9-12; pages 54-55 (Hist3, Hist4) C1 LP, C2 K-2, C3-C4 3-5, C5-C7 6-8, C8-C10 9-12. Standard statements, content-area headings and learning priorities apply to all bands (K-12). The History strand has an intro page of Historical Eras and Themes tables (Wisconsin, U.S., world) for K-12. No separate examples blocks: e.g./i.e. lists are inside indicators.
